critique: The notched, square-cut joint repeated on every strip is a genuinely unfamiliar grammar: the vermilion, cobalt and chartreuse bands step down in the same displaced stair, then re-emerge in front of the photograph as their own continuations. That rhymes intelligently with the slit-and-fold felt panel, and it keeps the whole sheet high-key on a pale citron ground. The weakness is that the motion, a 36-pixel ease-in-out sway, is the most conventional element on the page, and the stepped joints never slip, separate, or re-register, so the "passed from one material to another" idea stays static.
